<!--
  Front matter comes first, then the body. The boundary between them is the
  first level-1 heading, and the formatting stage finds it by style rather than
  by counting pages.

  The sources deliberately contain no page-number directives. Roman front matter
  and arabic body numbering require a *section break* between the two, and a
  section break is a property of the document rather than of the markdown: the
  formatting stage sets `w:pgNumType` per section, and `verify` checks that the
  format changes at most once and restarts at 1 when it does.

  A project that needs more than one section inserts the breaks in the imported
  front matter, which is where they belong -- the front matter is copied
  byte-for-byte precisely so that its section properties survive.
